messages:
maria: heads up — after the kernel-selector rollout (~14:03 UTC) p99 latency jumped to ~2.1s for gen endpoints. p50 looks fine. Anyone else seeing this?

james: saw the alert. is this all regions or just us-east-1? :eyes:

maria: mostly us-east-1 and one noisy node (gpu-12). grafana -> p99 heatmap linked.

ravi: did we change admission/microbatching config recently? last scheduler change touched dynamic_microbatching.

lina: KV cache eviction rate on gpu-12 jumped from 18k/s -> 160k/s around the deploy window. That smells like cache churn, not raw model kernel slowness.

theo: packing/kernel selection tweak in v2.4 increased packing aggressiveness (more aggressive kernel fusion). Could cause larger microbatches to be assembled which then thrash the KV cache under multi-tenant load.

maria: attaching quick tail flame: ```flamegraph snippet: main stall in kv_cache::lookup_hot_path -> 48% time; kernels still ~expected```. link: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/1954321000 (internal)

james: can we repro in staging? I can run a 25 qps mixed-length workload. If it's microbatch consolidation I should see similar kv eviction bump.

ravi: repro done: staging shows p99 ~900ms vs baseline 120ms when kernel-selector v2.4 + admission dynamic_n enabled. Logs: `admission: coalesced_microbatch_size=18` (baseline was 6).

lina: interesting — eviction-per-request metric goes up linearly with coalesced_microbatch_size. means each consolidated batch causes many KV evicts per token.

theo: thinking: kernel packing increases per-batch work and simultaneously admission lets microbatches grow, so per-request tail increases. With a noisy neighbor on same GPU it blows out p99.

maria: ops — can we cordon gpu-12 and drain affected pods while we triage?

ops-bot: INC created INC-4321. Tagged gpu-12. Cordon/drain in progress.

deploy-bot: kernel-selector v2.4 promoted to 100% at 14:03 UTC (canary->prod). rollback option available.

james: tactical: two short-term mitigations: 1) cap max_microbatch to 8 in admission controller 2) roll back kernel-selector to v2.3. Which do we want first?

ravi: I'd cap admission first (safer), validate, then rollback if cap doesn't recover p99. Cap command: `kubectl set env deployment/admission-controller MAX_MICROBATCH=8`.

maria: applying cap now.

lina: after cap: KV eviction dropped from 160k/s -> 26k/s on gpu-12, p99 down to ~300ms. Looks promising.

theo: still want to rollback kernel-selector to remove interaction risk. suggest canary rollback to v2.3 while we add tests.

maria: I kicked the rollback. deploy-bot acknowledged.

deploy-bot: rollback to kernel-selector v2.3 initiated (targeting all clusters).

james: after rollback and cap: p99 trending back to baseline across regions. recording timeline.

lina: follow-up action items: add metric `microbatch.consolidation_ratio` and `kv.evictions_per_microbatch`, add unit/regression tests for kernel-selector x admission combos, and add a gating perf test to CI that runs the mixed-length workload.

ravi: longer-term: scheduler should include a safety heuristic that prevents >N coalesced requests if node eviction rate spikes. I'll draft a proposal.

maria: owners: james -> kernel-selector revert/patch; lina -> KV metrics + dashboards; ravi -> admission safety heuristic + perf test. I'll draft a short postmortem and link to INC-4321.

theo: note for postmortem: call out multi-tenant risk and add guidance to prefer dedicated slots for high-throughput customers until packing heuristics are validated.

maria: great. closing loop here once postmortem + PRs are in. :thumbsup:
